column3: vt. 擦亮, 打磨, 磨光;vi. 磨光发亮
column5: The hotel spent millions to burnish its tarnished public image.
column6: 酒店斥资数百万修复受损的公众形象。

column3: a. 不能修补的, 不能挽回的;不可弥补的, 不可挽回的
column5: The scandal caused irreparable damage to the senator's reputation.
column6: 丑闻给参议员的名誉造成无可挽回的损害。

column3: vt. 劈开, 分开;vi. 劈开, 分开, 粘着, 依恋
column5: Loggers use steel wedges to cleave the oak trunks along the grain.
column6: 伐木工用钢楔顺纹理劈开橡木树干。

column3: vt. 剥夺...的公民权, 使失去法律保护, 把...充军, 把...放逐, 排斥, 禁止
column5: New regulations proscribe the use of certain pesticides near schools.
column6: 新法规禁止在学校附近使用某些杀虫剂。

column3: n. 吵闹声, 叫嚷声, 混乱
column5: The hubbub of the trading floor faded as the closing bell rang.
column6: 收盘钟响起,交易大厅的嘈杂渐渐平息。

column3: a. 单色的, 单频的;单色的
column5: The artist chose a monochromatic palette of blues for the series.
column6: 艺术家为该系列选用了单一的蓝色调。

column3: n. 刺绣, 缝纫
column5: Her grandmother's intricate needlework still hangs framed in the hallway.
column6: 祖母做工精细的刺绣还装裱着挂在走廊。

column3: a. 不知疲倦的, 有耐性的, 不屈不挠的
column5: The indefatigable volunteer has delivered meals to shut-ins every day for years.
column6: 这位不知疲倦的志愿者多年来每天给行动不便者送餐。

column3: n. 平版印刷品, 石版画;vt. 以平版印刷
column5: A rare lithograph of the old city sold for thousands at auction.
column6: 一幅罕见的旧城石版画在拍卖会上拍出数千美元。

column3: adv. 不规律地, 不定地
column5: The old truck has been running erratically since the flood.
column6: 洪水过后,那辆旧卡车一直忽好忽坏。

column3: n. 喉头;喉
column5: Smoking can seriously damage the larynx and deepen the voice.
column6: 吸烟会严重损害喉部,让嗓音变得低沉。

column3: vt. 办理, 处理;vi. 作交易, 谈判
column5: Most of the trade between the firms is transacted through licensed brokers.
column6: 两家公司之间的交易大多通过持牌经纪商完成。

column3: n. 推进剂, 发射火药, 推进者;火药
column5: The rocket's propellant ignited six seconds before liftoff.
column6: 火箭的推进剂在升空前六秒点火。

column3: v. 游手好闲, 混日子
column5: Tourists who dawdle in the square miss the last cable car.
column6: 在广场上磨蹭的游客会错过末班缆车。

column3: n. 虚弱, 病身, 疾病;衰弱
column5: Despite his growing infirmity, the professor still lectures twice a week.
column6: 尽管身体日渐衰弱,教授仍坚持每周讲两次课。

column3: n. 针头, 小东西, 微不足道的东西
column5: The sensor is smaller than a pinhead yet performs a billion calculations.
column6: 这种传感器比针尖还小,却能进行十亿次运算。

column3: n. 慌乱, 激动, 紧张不安;vt. 使紧张, 使慌张, 使激动
column5: Unexpected questions from the floor can fluster even seasoned speakers.
column6: 台下突如其来的提问连资深演讲者也会慌乱。

column3: a. 不屈服的, 不屈不挠的
column5: Her indomitable spirit carried the startup through its darkest year.
column6: 她不屈的精神带领初创公司熬过最黑暗的一年。

column3: n. 不动性, 不动, 固定;不动
column5: Prolonged immobility on long flights raises the risk of blood clots.
column6: 长途飞行中久坐不动会增加血栓风险。

column3: a. 令人憎恨的, 可恶的, 厌恶的, 相抵触的, 不一致的
column5: The leaked memo described practices that many readers found abhorrent.
column6: 泄露的备忘录描述的做法令许多读者深恶痛绝。

column3: vt. 缩写, 使...简略, 缩短;vi. 使用缩写词
column5: Please abbreviate the chemical names to save space in the table.
column6: 请缩写这些化学名称,以节省表格空间。

column3: n. 收缩, 收缩量, 减低;起皱; 收缩; 收缩量
column5: High heat causes noticeable shrinkage in woolen garments.
column6: 高温会使毛料衣物明显缩水。

column3: n. 海星
column5: A starfish moved slowly across the bottom of the tide pool.
column6: 一只海星在潮池底部缓缓移动。

column3: a. 博学的;n. 博学者
column5: The erudite professor can quote medieval poetry in four languages.
column6: 这位博学的教授能用四种语言背诵中世纪诗歌。

column3: a. 不自私的, 无我的, 不谋私利的
column5: Her unselfish decision to share the credit won everyone's respect.
column6: 她主动分享功劳的无私之举赢得众人敬意。

column3: n. 离题, 扯到枝节上, 偏离
column5: After a long digression about his youth, the lecturer returned to macroeconomics.
column6: 离题大谈年轻往事后,讲师回到宏观经济学。

column3: vi. 默许, 共谋, 纵容;默许, 纵容, 共谋
column5: Several officials connived to hide the losses from the auditors.
column6: 几名官员串通向审计人员隐瞒亏损。

column3: n. 征服, 服从, 隶属;隶属, 服从, 屈从
column5: The empire held conquered peoples in subjection for over two centuries.
column6: 帝国将被征服民族压制统治了两百多年。

column3: n. 忠诚, 诚实, 正确
column5: The dog's faithfulness to its injured owner moved the rescue team.
column6: 狗对受伤主人的忠诚感动了救援人员。

column3: a. 难辨认的, 字迹模糊的
column5: His application was rejected because the signature was completely illegible.
column6: 申请被驳回,因为签名完全无法辨认。
